groups.intro:
Whether and how the state credentials this profession — the regulatory model,
credential type, issuing authority, entry requirements (education, exams, age,
character), fees, renewal, continuing education, and reciprocity.

fields.meaning: Whether the state requires a credential to practice this profession.

example.quote: An individual may not, unless licensed as a dietitian or nutritionist by the department, use the title "dietitian," "licensed dietitian," "nutritionist," "licensed nutritionist," or an occupational ti

fields.meaning: Free-text name of the board/agency that issues the credential (the structured form is `regulatory_authority`).

example.value: Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development
example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development

fields.meaning: Structured decomposition of the issuing authority — name, type (standalone board / shared board / division / department / joint), and any umbrella agency it sits within. Populated alongside the legacy free-text issuing_authority for back-compat.
Canonical name of the immediate authority (e.g., 'State Board of Podiatry').

example.value: Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development
example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development

fields.meaning: Structural classification of the immediate authority.

example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development

fields.meaning: Higher-level agency that contains the immediate authority, if any. Example: 'Division of Occupations and Professions, Department of Commerce'. Null for standalone boards that don't sit inside a larger department.

example.quote: "Department" means the Department of Health.

fields.meaning: Minimum age (years) to hold the credential, if the statute sets one.

example.quote: Be 19 years of age or older.

fields.meaning: Whether the statute conditions licensure on good moral character / fitness.

example.quote: Submit evidence of good moral character and respectability.

fields.meaning: Education entry requirement — degree, level, accreditation, and any tiers.

example.value: master's or doctoral degree from an accredited college or university with a major in human nutrition, public health nutrition, clinical nutrition, nutrition education, community nutrition, or food and nutrition
example.quote: has received a master's or doctoral degree from an accredited college or university with a major in human nutrition, public health nutrition, clinical nutrition, nutrition education, community nutriti

example.value: regional or national accrediting agencies recognized by the Council on Post-Secondary Accreditation and the United States Department of Education
example.quote: "accredited college or university" means a college or university accredited by the regional or national accrediting agencies recognized by the Council on Post-Secondary Accreditation and the United St

fields.meaning: The comparable education FLOOR as a normalized rung. Populate whenever licensure is gated on a degree; null only if the statute is silent on education.

example.quote: has received a master's or doctoral degree from an accredited college or university

fields.meaning: How the statute decides a school counts. national_accreditor=a named national program accreditor (ACOE/CODA/ACEND/LCME/CPME). regional_accreditor='regionally accredited college or university'. board_approved='approved by the board' (discretionary state gate). unspecified=says 'accredited' with no basis named, or silent.

example.quote: accredited by the regional or national accrediting agencies recognized by the Council on Post-Secondary Accreditation and the United States Department of Education

fields.meaning: True if the statute pegs the education requirement to a NATIONAL CREDENTIAL (e.g. 'registered by CDR', 'passed the NBEO') rather than (or in addition to) a stated degree — such a state inherits whatever that national body currently requires.

example.quote: submits evidence satisfactory to the department of being certified as a Registered Dietitian by the Commission on Dietetic Registration

fields.meaning: Per-tier floors when the statute sets different education levels for different license classes, or phases the floor in by date. Omit/null when there is a single floor. `degree_level` still records the overall floor across all tiers.
Which class/date this floor applies to — e.g. 'licensed dietitian', 'certified nutritionist', 'applicants on or after 2024-01-01'.

Normalized education floor, low -> high. Resolved to the rung even when
the statute uses verbiage ('six college years' -> doctorate, 'or equivalent
degree' -> the named level). Professional/clinical doctorates (OD, DDS, MD,
DPM) are `doctorate`.
ISO date when this floor takes effect, for date-phased tiers (e.g. '2024-01-01'). Null otherwise.
Supervised practice / residency / apprenticeship required after the degree.

example.quote: has completed a documented work experience in human nutrition or human nutrition research of at least 900 hours

fields.meaning: ALWAYS populate (required_by_statute / embedded_in_credential / none) unless the governing statute is absent from the corpus. Disambiguates a blank `required`: 'none' (truly no requirement) vs 'embedded_in_credential' (the accredited degree the statute points to carries the supervised hours).

example.quote: has completed a documented work experience in human nutrition or human nutrition research of at least 900 hours

fields.meaning: e.g. '24 months', '1 year', '2,000 hours' (free text — units vary)

example.quote: has completed a documented work experience in human nutrition or human nutrition research of at least 900 hours

fields.meaning: e.g. 'podiatric residency', 'accounting work experience', 'AXP'

example.value: documented work experience in human nutrition or human nutrition research
example.quote: documented work experience in human nutrition or human nutrition research of at least 900 hours

fields.meaning: Examinations required for the credential (one entry per exam).

example.value: Waived if applicant provides evidence of current CDR registration as a registered dietitian.

fields.meaning: Where the exam is administered / who owns it — e.g. 'NBPME (national)', 'state board (in-state)', 'NCLEX-RN (national)'. Use the statute's language; null if the source doesn't say.
Max attempts allowed before re-qualification. Null if not specified.
How the credential is renewed — interval and any conditions.
Most states are 1 or 2

example.quote: Licenses shall be renewed biennially on the dates set by the department with the approval of the respective board.

fields.meaning: License renewal fee in US dollars (integer). Many statutes leave the amount to the board's discretion — leave null in that case.

example.quote: payment of a renewal fee of one hundred five dollars

fields.meaning: Continuing-education requirement to keep the credential active.

example.quote: An applicant for renewal of a license must have satisfactorily maintained continuing education requirements through the Commission on Dietetic Registration or as specified and approved by the board.
Thirty hours of continuing education are required during the 2-year licensure period.
Thirty hours of continuing education are required during the 2-year licensure period.

fields.meaning: Specific topical CE requirements, e.g. ['1.5 hrs opioid', 'ethics']

example.quote: the department, in consultation with the board, shall promulgate rules requiring each applicant for license renewal to complete as part of the continuing education required under subsection (1) an app

fields.meaning: Whether/how the state recognizes out-of-state credentials (endorsement/reciprocity).

example.quote: The department may issue a license to an applicant who holds a current unrestricted license as a dietitian or nutritionist in another state or political jurisdiction of the United States or Canada if,

fields.meaning: Free-form summary

example.value: Applicant must hold a current unrestricted license as a dietitian or nutritionist in another state or political jurisdiction of the United States or Canada, and the department must find those standards are not less stringent than Alaska's requirements.
example.quote: holds a current unrestricted license as a dietitian or nutritionist in another state or political jurisdiction of the United States or Canada if, in the judgment of the department, the standards for l

fields.meaning: Profession-specific advisory body sitting alongside the main licensing board, when one exists. Populated for states that delegate licensure to a generic board and add a specialty advisory committee.
True if a profession-specific advisory body exists alongside the main licensing board. False if the licensing board itself is profession-specific (no separate advisory body needed).

example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development

fields.meaning: Name of the advisory board, e.g. 'Podiatry Advisory Committee'.

example.quote: There is created the Dietetics and Nutrition Practice Council under the supervision of the board.

fields.meaning: Authority the advisory board has, in the statute's own words — e.g. 'advisory only', 'rulemaking subject to board approval', 'disciplinary recommendations'. Free text from the statute.

example.value: The board may delegate such powers and duties to the council as it may deem proper to carry out the operations and procedures necessary to effectuate the provisions of this part.
example.quote: The board may delegate such powers and duties to the council as it may deem proper to carry out the operations and procedures necessary to effectuate the provisions of this part.

fields.meaning: Name of a national CERTIFICATION the state recognizes or requires, e.g. 'American Board of Podiatric Surgery (ABPS)' or 'National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners (NBPME)'. The certifying body, NOT the association. Null if the statute doesn't reference one.

example.quote: submits evidence satisfactory to the department of being certified as a Registered Dietitian by the Commission on Dietetic Registration

fields.meaning: Professional ASSOCIATION the state references (e.g. for accreditation or CE provider approval) — 'American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA)', 'American Dental Association (ADA)'. Distinct from the certifying body. Null if not referenced.

example.quote: "Commission on Dietetic Registration" means the Commission on Dietetic Registration of the American Dietetic Association

fields.meaning: Which UORF model the state applies to this profession (license / mandatory_cert / registration / etc).

example.quote: An individual may not, unless licensed as a dietitian or nutritionist by the department, use the title "dietitian," "licensed dietitian," "nutritionist," "licensed nutritionist," or an occupational ti

fields.meaning: What SHAPE of credential does the state issue, independent of whether holding it is mandatory? license / certification / registration / exemption / none. Pairs with is_mandatory to decompose the legacy regulatory_model rung.

example.quote: The department shall issue a dietitian license to an individual who pays the required fee, applies on a form provided by the department

fields.meaning: Is the credential MANDATORY to practice (or claim the title) in this state? True if practicing without it is prohibited; False if optional (e.g., voluntary certification that only protects the title for those who hold it).

example.quote: An individual may not, unless licensed as a dietitian or nutritionist by the department, use the title "dietitian," "licensed dietitian," "nutritionist," "licensed nutritionist," or an occupational ti

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict use of the profession's title to licensees? True if unlicensed people may NOT call themselves the protected title (e.g. 'podiatrist', 'CPA').

example.quote: An individual may not, unless licensed as a dietitian or nutritionist by the department, use the title "dietitian," "licensed dietitian," "nutritionist," "licensed nutritionist," or an occupational ti

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict practice of the profession's scope to licensees? True if performing the scope without a license is prohibited (independent of title use).

example.quote: An individual may not, unless licensed as a dietitian or nutritionist by the department, use the title "dietitian," "licensed dietitian," "nutritionist," "licensed nutritionist," or an occupational ti

fields.meaning: Grounds on which the board may discipline a licensee. Typical statutes list 5-15.
snake_case key, e.g. 'fraud_in_obtaining_license'
One-line plain-English description

example.value: Secured or attempted to secure a license through deceit, fraud, or intentional misrepresentation

fields.meaning: Non-credential regulatory mechanisms (bonding, insurance, establishment regulation) imposed by the state. Obama 2015 framework typology. Independent of credential_type.
Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to post a bond (funds against which consumer claims can be made)? Independent of whether a credential is also required.
Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to carry insurance (e.g., professional liability, surety insurance)?
Does the statute regulate the ESTABLISHMENT / FIRM (e.g., facility license, mandatory inspection of premises) as a route to consumer protection, independent of any practitioner credential?
Statutory citations supporting the licensure fields above.

groups.intro:
What the practice act lets (or reserves to) this profession — the defined scope,
authorized methods, drug authority, and any title/scope protection. Skeleton only —
profession-specific scope richness lives in the discovered block.

fields.meaning: Verbatim statutory definition; quote field repeats the value text.

example.value: the integration and application of scientific principles of food, nutrition, biochemistry, physiology, food management, and behavioral and social sciences to achieve and maintain human health through the provision of nutrition care services
example.quote: "dietetics or nutrition practice" means the integration and application of scientific principles of food, nutrition, biochemistry, physiology, food management, and behavioral and social sciences to ac

fields.meaning: High-level methods, e.g. ['medical','surgical','mechanical']

value: Assessing nutritional needs of individuals and groups
Establishing priorities, goals, and objectives that meet nutritional needs
Providing nutrition counseling in health and disease
Developing, implementing, and managing nutrition care systems
Evaluating, making changes in, and maintaining appropriate standards of quality in food and nutrition services
example.quote: The primary function of dietetic practice is the provision of nutrition care services which shall include: (1) Assessing the nutritional needs of individuals and groups... (2) Establishing priorities,

fields.meaning: Whether/how the profession may prescribe, administer, or dispense drugs.

example.value: Dietitian nutritionist may implement prescription drug dose adjustments for specific disease treatment protocols under approved protocols and under delegation of a prescriber; may not prescribe or initiate drug treatment independently.
example.quote: Except as otherwise provided in this section, the dietitian nutritionist shall not prescribe or initiate drug treatment.

fields.meaning: Statutory citations supporting the scope fields above.

groups.intro: Fields discovered specifically for this profession (auto-derived from its statutes); they vary profession to profession.

fields.meaning: The distinct credential or license types recognized by the state (e.g., licensed dietitian, licensed nutritionist, dietitian-nutritionist, registered dietitian, provisionally licensed dietitian).

example.quote: The department shall issue a dietitian license to an individual... The department shall issue a nutritionist license to an individual

fields.meaning: Whether the state offers a provisional or temporary license allowing practice under supervision while completing full licensure requirements.

example.quote: A temporary license to practice as a dietitian/nutritionist may be issued by the board upon the filing of an application and submission of evidence of successful completion of education requirements s

fields.meaning: Duration in months of a provisional or temporary license before it expires.

example.quote: A temporary license shall expire one year from the date of issuance.

fields.meaning: Whether a provisional or temporary license restricts the holder to practice only under the supervision of a fully licensed dietitian.

example.quote: A provisional license shall permit the holder to practice only under the supervision of a dietitian licensed in this state.

fields.meaning: Whether the state statute explicitly recognizes a dietetic technician credential as a distinct, lower-tier role that may perform limited functions under supervision.

example.quote: DIETETIC TECHNICIAN. A person who is trained to perform specific dietetic functions of a licensed dietitian/nutritionist as defined by this chapter under the direct supervision of a licensed dietitian

fields.meaning: Whether holding a current Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN) credential from the Commission on Dietetic Registration is explicitly accepted as satisfying all or most state licensure requirements.

example.quote: submits evidence satisfactory to the department of being certified as a Registered Dietitian by the Commission on Dietetic Registration

fields.meaning: Non-RD national credentials or membership bodies that the state accepts as an alternative pathway to licensure (e.g., Certified Nutrition Specialist, American Board of Nutrition diplomate).

value: Diplomate of the American Board of Nutrition
Certified Nutrition Specialist with the Certification Board for Nutrition Specialists
example.quote: has qualified as a diplomate of the American Board of Nutrition or as a Certified Nutrition Specialist with the Certification Board for Nutrition Specialists

fields.meaning: Whether the statute explicitly authorizes the practice of 'medical nutrition therapy' as part of the dietitian's scope.

example.quote: PRACTICE OF DIETETICS. The synthesis and application of dietetics, primarily for the provision of nutrition care services, including medical nutrition therapy

fields.meaning: Whether the statute explicitly includes ordering or recommending enteral and/or parenteral nutrition within the dietitian's scope of practice.

example.quote: NUTRITIONAL ASSESSMENT. The evaluation of the nutritional needs of individuals and groups based upon appropriate biochemical, anthropometric, physical, and dietary data to determine nutrient needs and

fields.meaning: Whether the statute explicitly grants dietitians authority to write or issue diet orders (including therapeutic diets) in institutional or hospital settings.

example.quote: A hospital that is licensed pursuant to section 36-422 may allow a registered dietitian or other qualified nutrition professional to order diets

fields.meaning: Whether the statute explicitly grants dietitians authority to order medical laboratory tests related to nutrition therapy.

example.quote: a registered dietitian, or other nutritional professional meeting the qualifications set forth in subdivision (e) of Section 2585, may order medical laboratory tests related to medical nutrition thera

fields.meaning: Whether the statute requires a physician (or other authorized prescriber) referral or order before a dietitian may provide certain clinical nutrition services.

example.quote: a dietitian/nutritionist or registered dietitian meeting the qualifications set forth in Section 34-34-1, may, upon referral by a health care provider authorized to prescribe dietary treatments

fields.meaning: Whether the statute explicitly prohibits dietitians from diagnosing, treating, or prescribing for human illness or otherwise practicing medicine.

example.quote: a person licensed to practice dietetics/nutrition or to provide nutritional care services shall not diagnose, treat, or prescribe for any human illness, injury, disease, impairment, or infirmity, or o

fields.meaning: Whether the statute explicitly authorizes dietitians to provide services via telehealth.

example.quote: PRACTICE OF DIETETICS. The synthesis and application of dietetics, primarily for the provision of nutrition care services, including medical nutrition therapy, in person or via telehealth

fields.meaning: Maximum number of dietetic technicians a single registered dietitian may supervise at one time.

example.quote: a registered dietitian shall not supervise more than two dietetic technicians, registered at one time.

fields.meaning: Whether the statute provides an explicit definition of 'direct supervision' for dietetic technicians or provisional licensees, including physical presence or availability requirements.

example.quote: DIETETIC TECHNICIAN. A person who is trained to perform specific dietetic functions of a licensed dietitian/nutritionist as defined by this chapter under the direct supervision of a licensed dietitian

fields.meaning: Categories of other licensed professionals explicitly exempted from the dietetics licensure requirement when performing nutrition-related activities incidental to their own profession.

value: Animal nutritionist (nutrition care of animals only)
Federal government employee whose job title includes 'dietitian' or 'nutritionist'
Person serving as a dietitian or nutritionist in the armed forces of the United States
example.quote: The requirements of this chapter do not apply to (1) an animal nutritionist whose activities are limited to the nutritional care of animals; (2) a person who is serving as an employee of the federal g

fields.meaning: Whether persons employed by the federal government (including armed forces, VA, or public health service) in a dietitian or nutritionist role are explicitly exempt from state licensure.

example.quote: a person who is serving as an employee of the federal government whose job title includes the term "dietitian" or "nutritionist"

fields.meaning: Whether persons offering weight control programs are explicitly exempt from licensure, typically conditioned on the program being reviewed or approved by a licensed or registered dietitian.

example.quote: Any person who provides weight control services provided the program has been reviewed by a dietitian/nutritionist as defined in this chapter and consultation is available from a dietitian/nutritionis

fields.meaning: Whether persons who sell, market, or provide information about food, dietary supplements, vitamins, or herbs are explicitly exempt from the dietetics licensure requirement.

example.quote: Nothing in this chapter is intended to prohibit any person who does not hold himself or herself out to be a dietitian or nutritionist from furnishing general nutritional information on food, food mate

fields.meaning: Whether persons whose nutrition practice is limited to animals are explicitly exempt from the human dietetics licensure requirement.

example.quote: an animal nutritionist whose activities are limited to the nutritional care of animals; animal nutritionists may use the title "nutritionist" as long as they provide nutrition services only to animals

fields.meaning: Whether out-of-state dietitians may practice in the state for a limited period without obtaining a state license.

example.quote: A nonresident dietitian practicing dietetics in this state, if: (A) The dietetics are performed for no more than one hundred eighty (180) consecutive working days

fields.meaning: Maximum number of days per year a nonresident dietitian may practice in the state without a state license.

example.quote: The dietetics are performed for no more than one hundred eighty (180) consecutive working days

fields.meaning: Whether the state has enacted the Dietitian Licensure Compact, enabling multistate practice privileges.

example.quote: The compact member states hereby create and establish a joint governmental agency whose membership consists of all member states that have enacted the compact known as the Dietitian Licensure Compact

fields.meaning: Whether a state may require applicants for a compact practice privilege to pass a jurisprudence (state law knowledge) assessment.

example.quote: Meet any jurisprudence requirements established by the remote state in which the licensee is seeking a compact privilege

fields.meaning: The specific titles, words, letters, or abbreviations that are legally restricted to licensed or certified practitioners under the statute.

example.quote: use the title "dietitian," "licensed dietitian," "nutritionist," "licensed nutritionist," or an occupational title using the word "dietitian" or "nutritionist."

fields.meaning: Whether the statutory definition of nutritional assessment explicitly includes biochemical and anthropometric data as evaluation components.

example.quote: NUTRITIONAL ASSESSMENT. The evaluation of the nutritional needs of individuals and groups based upon appropriate biochemical, anthropometric, physical, and dietary data

fields.meaning: Whether a dietitian's authority to issue orders in a hospital setting is conditioned on the hospital having written policies and procedures authorizing such orders.

example.quote: The hospital's written policies and procedures allow registered dietitians or other qualified nutrition professionals to issue such orders.

fields.meaning: Whether the state allows a licensee to place their license in an inactive status for a defined period.

example.quote: A license under this part which has become inactive may be reactivated pursuant to this section.

fields.meaning: Whether violation of a recognized professional code of ethics (e.g., the American Dietetic Association's code) is explicitly listed as a ground for disciplinary action.

example.quote: Has violated the Code of Ethics as established by the American Dietetic Association
example.citation: § 3811. Grounds for discipline/sanctions/penalties of unlicensed practice.
